provider: Blossom server fleet (24242.io, blossom.oslim.dev / Lotus, blossom.nostr.build)

free_tier.stated: 24242.io 100 MiB/file, deleted if not accessed for 60 days. blossom.oslim.dev (Lotus): 100 MB/file and 8 GB per pubkey, retention 'permanent', cost 'free'. blossom.nostr.build: 20 MiB/file free tier, 'no limit on how many files, and no expiry'.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: 24242.io 100 MiB/file, deleted if not accessed for 60 days

egress.terms: unmetered / CDN-fronted. nostr.build advertises 'Global CDN delivery' on free uploads.

tooling: curl; hzrd149/blossom CLI; any Blossom client. BUD-04 `/mirror` lets one server pull a blob from another given a URL, so replication is a server-side call, not a client re-upload.
chaining: aggregate GB is the sum over the fleet x number of keypairs (oslim's 8 GB is per-pubkey, and pubkeys cost nothing). 24242.io's 60-day access-based retention is defeated by any periodic HEAD.

limits.value: deleted if not accessed for 60 days

limits_note: per-object-cap 100 MiB on most servers (20 MiB on nostr.build free). This is chunk-sized, not object-sized. 24242.io caps /list at the first 250 hits, so enumeration needs date ranges.
reliability_note: small volunteer hosts, several with unstated total capacity. 24242.io states 'Free and unrestricted... for now'. Prefer BUD-04 mirroring to two servers per chunk.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

extras.agent_focus: Relay/P2P transport networks that could carry bulk data without a central provider. For each: is data ROUTED (a real path) or is it only SIGNALLING (relay coordinates, bytes go peer-to-peer)? Free bandwidth? Can it carry 1 TiB/day (= 12.7 MB/s = ~102 Mbit/s sustained)? Identity gate recorded as the primary ranking axis.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
